The core innovation lies in replacing traditional one-hot encodings with a geometric mapping to the unit circle. This transformation eliminates combinatorial singular hyperplanes that plague score-based diffusion models. Each categorical value maps to a unique point on the circle, preserving order while enabling smooth interpolation. In GSI, this allows ordinal inference over team rankings, where prior strength is encoded continuously. For GSE, the same principle applies to state transitions—team identities, venue types, and temporal sequences are embedded into a continuous space, enabling efficient flow matching. The elimination of singularities ensures stable gradient computation and improved convergence. The mathematical foundation rests on the fact that the sum of unit vectors forms a central point, collapsing the exponential complexity of one-hot spaces into manageable linear structures.
